diagnosis: The scenario fails because checks C3 and C5 are satisfied by the model's default tendency to flag missing disclosures or compliance requirements when presented with any financial reporting context. Specifically, C3 (linked to PF1) passes because the model correctly identifies that 'eparate_presentation_required' should be true for complex programs, even though it lacks the specific PF1 fact. Similarly, C5 (linked to PF2) passes because the model defaults 'quarterly_supplier_finance_certification_required' to true as a generic compliance measure.

C3.why: The draft treats the amounts as ordinary trade payables with no separate disclosure; PF1 changes accounting_classification to supplier_finance_obligation, turns separate_presentation_required on, and sets maximum_outstanding_balance_disclosed_usd to exactly 6000000.

C5.why: The draft contains no special certification control; PF2 changes quarterly_supplier_finance_certification_required to true, sets certification_due_days_after_quarter_end to exactly 10, and requires the quarterly_certification commitment.
